name: Martha 'Mattie' Grindle
languages: Gloucester Portuguese, enough to swear and to bargain
equipment: Heavy coat: yellow oilskins over a fisherman's jersey, a sou'wester, and thigh boots
Double-barrel shotgun (a ten-gauge her grandfather used for sea ducks, older than she is), kept in the fish shed
Kitchen knife, a short bait knife she keeps in her boot and uses for everything
A twenty-foot lobster boat, the Rhoda G., with a make-and-break engine, two hundred traps and a dory
A bucket of salt herring bait, a gaff, a coil of pot warp and a lantern
Her grandmother Lois's hymnbook, with a list of names written in the back in pencil, in an old woman's hand, headed 'Point folk, 1871'
features: Up Before Dawn (Farm-Raised origin: needs only 6 hours for a long rest; can't be surprised while awake in the last hour before sunrise; advantage on saves against exhaustion from hard work, cold and lost sleep; notices without a check when animals are frightened, sick or behaving wrongly). Fishing hours are farm hours: she is on the water by four

Hard to Kill (Roughneck: once per long rest, when reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, she drops to 1 instead; ignores her first level of exhaustion; advantage on CON saves against exhaustion, cold and hard labor)
Heavy Work (Roughneck: advantage on STR checks to lift, push, pull, break or force something; counts as one size larger for carrying and dragging; carries an unconscious adult at full speed)

Bull-Headed (Roughneck, 2nd level: once per short rest, when she fails a fear check, she gains no Dread but must move toward the source on her next turn and attack it or break what stands between them, or smash something nearby)

Trade: Longshoreman (Roughneck, 3rd level: advantage on Athletics checks to grapple, shove or hold a door, and a creature she grapples has disadvantage on checks to escape; she is the person you want holding someone back from the water)

Nobody's Business (Drifter background: she worked the Gloucester wharves and the Lubec sardine sheds and knows how to travel the coast for nothing; drifters, deckhands and cannery hands share news with her; and when a stranger goes missing, nobody asks)

personality.traits: I say what I think in as few words as it'll go in. I haul two hundred traps a day by hand and I don't see why anyone else can't. I go very still when somebody says the word 'Proprietors'.
personality.ideals: The Point was ours. The houses, the net stands, the flakes, the fishing. My great-grandfather Thomas Grindle paid rent on it for thirty years and they took it off a dead man. I'm not after anybody's blood. I want it said out loud.
personality.bonds: My grandmother Lois Grindle, who was eighteen miles off on the mainland in service the night the Point went down, and whose mother and father were in the church; she died in 1915 and told me the story nobody believed. My boat. Peleg Sprague, which is nobody's business.
personality.flaws: I am angry at the whole island, and the whole island can tell. I would rather be right than be liked, and I usually manage it. I do not trust anyone named Sprague, Wyman, Coombs, Farr or Tibbetts, and that is half the island and one of them is Peleg.

appearance: A big, square-shouldered woman of thirty-four with a wind-reddened face, straight black brows, dark hair in a braid under a sou'wester, a broken nose she got off a winch, and forearms like a man's. Oilskins, thigh boots, a bait knife in the boot top, and a smell of herring that she says is the smell of honest money.
backstory: Mattie Grindle is the last of the Point Grindles on Carrow. Her great-grandparents, Thomas and Rhoda Grindle, died in the church in 1871; their daughter Lois, then nineteen and in service in a Rockland house, came home to find her parents, her house and her family's fishing privilege gone, the first two to the sea and the third, through the probate court and a bill for unpaid rent, to Captain Hezekiah Sprague. Lois married a Harbor fisherman and lived and died on Carrow, and told her granddaughter Mattie, over and over, that the Proprietors 'shut them in and let them drown', which nobody on the island believed, because Lois was a sharp-tongued old woman who did not like the Spragues. Mattie went away at seventeen and worked the Gloucester fish wharves and the Lubec sardine factories for ten years, and came home at twenty-seven when her father died, to haul his traps. She is a fine lobsterman, the best boat-handler in the Harbor after Galen Coombs and Oren Pinkham, and the only person on Carrow who will go out to the Bar on a big tide at night, because the bell never calls a Grindle. She has been seeing Peleg Sprague, very quietly, since the summer.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Mattie is the voice of the people who died, and she does not know how right she is. Her grandmother's list of 'Point folk, 1871' in the back of the hymnbook is one of the five sources for the names (CLUE F4), and her grandmother's story is the first time the party hears the word 'shut'. She will row or motor the party anywhere, knows the Bar and the Point's channels in any light, and is fearless on the water and on the Point because she is not of the blood; she is the obvious person to send out onto the Shelf, and the party should feel the irony that she is going to open the doors the Proprietors spiked on her family. She is strong, blunt and useful in a fight, and absolutely loyal once she trusts someone. She never wants anyone hurt; when the dead come ashore in the storm, she is the first to understand that they are her family.
dmNotes.voice: Down East, flat and short, 'ayuh' and 'nope' and 'some'. Doesn't ask questions, makes statements and waits. Swears in Gloucester Portuguese when the engine stalls.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: the truth said out loud, before the island, by a Proprietor. Secondary: the Point's fishing privilege given back to the Point families, which on Carrow now means her. Tertiary: keep Peleg from walking into the sea.
dmNotes.secrets: Her grandmother's list has twenty-two names on it, not twenty-three: Lois never knew one of the Gloucester men's names. Mattie also has a tintype of Thomas and Rhoda Grindle, which she will put in the drowned church if she gets there, and she has told Peleg the whole of her grandmother's story, which is why he believes Orpha.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: suspicious, then practical, then fierce. Toward Peleg: hidden tenderness and open teasing. Toward Ellery Wyman: open contempt. Toward Orpha Sprague: a long cold silence that has lasted twenty years. Toward Galen Coombs: business respect; she does not run his cases and he does not ask her to.
